project: QORE-VLM DPR positive-context gold alignment audit

baseline.entry_point: nq_open -> official DPR NQ-test gold context -> Wiki-DPR Top-50 -> frozen QORE + Answer Scorer Top-5
baseline.equivalence_test: The audit observes canonical IDs after frozen Top-50 retrieval and frozen QORE Top-5 selection; no diagnostic value is provided to the online path.

core_invariants: Official DPR positives are evaluation-only and never reach retrieval, QORE, prompts, Generator, or evaluator.
The nq_open validation[200:250] slice, official DPR nq-test_gold_info source, Wiki-DPR psgs_w100.nq.compressed Top-50, QORE K=5, DPR Answer Scorer, and seed=42 are frozen.
A strict question mapping requires normalized exact question identity and unique Wiki-DPR identity for every official DPR positive context.
A cheap question-join preflight must show that enough target questions join to reach the 0.80 mapping gate; otherwise the run stops before Wiki-DPR or model loading.
Compact results retain only identifiers, counts, booleans, source fingerprints, and manifests; they contain no question, passage, answer, title, text, prompt, or prediction content.

interfaces.input_schema: nq_open question and official DPR question
interfaces.output_schema: normalized exact join status and positive-context set
invariants: Question content is used only in process memory for the join and is never emitted.

interfaces.input_schema: official DPR nq-test_gold_info JSON object with data rows (adapted to positive-context records)
interfaces.output_schema: target-slice positive passage IDs and normalized title/full-text SHA-256 identities
invariants: The official source URL, local byte count, SHA-256, and retained record count are recorded in the run manifest.

interfaces.input_schema: full Wiki-DPR id/title/text rows and target positive identities
interfaces.output_schema: per-question verified canonical passage-ID set, full positive accounting, and identity methods
invariants: A partially mapped positive set is not strict mapped coverage.

interfaces.input_schema: frozen Top-50 IDs, frozen QORE Top-5 IDs, and completed offline alignment
interfaces.output_schema: compact Top-50/Top-5 gold coverage counts and booleans
invariants: The observer runs after selection and cannot alter any online decision.

plugins.hypothesis: Normalized exact question identity can join the frozen nq_open slice to the official DPR NQ-test gold source without heuristic matching.

plugins.insertion_point: offline source preparation before corpus scan
plugins.hypothesis: The official DPR positive contexts provide a more traceable gold-evidence source than v1 page-title/short-span matching.
plugins.output_schema: positive passage identity records for the target slice
plugins.resource_estimate: one streamed/read-only 1.4 MB compressed NQ-test source read; target records only retained in memory

plugins.hypothesis: Official DPR positives can be uniquely verified against the current Wiki-DPR corpus by official passage ID, normalized title plus full-text hash, or a unique full-text hash.
plugins.input_schema: Wiki-DPR rows and DPR positive identities
plugins.resource_estimate: one full Wiki-DPR metadata scan; no generation calls

plugins.insertion_point: after unchanged Top-50 retrieval and unchanged QORE Top-5 selection
plugins.hypothesis: After the mapping coverage gate passes, the difference between Top-50 and Top-5 coverage can discriminate retrieval loss from selection loss.
plugins.input_schema: canonical global IDs and completed alignment index
plugins.output_schema: compact per-question coverage measurements and gated summary

composition.merge_rule: Only canonical IDs and aggregate counts cross observer stages; no positive-context value crosses into retrieval, QORE, prompt construction, Generator, or evaluation.
interaction_ablations: official passage-ID match versus title/full-text hash match versus unique full-text hash match
strict all-positive mapping versus partial-positive accounting
frozen Top-50 coverage versus frozen QORE Top-5 coverage

validation.baseline_equivalence: Synthetic fixtures prove that offline label alignment changes only compact observer output; the frozen Top-50 and QORE Top-5 IDs remain inputs, never controls.
tests: normalized exact question join and duplicate conflict handling
official passage ID, title/full-text hash, and unique full-text identity matching
partial-positive exclusion from strict mapping coverage
question-join preflight and early-stop before Wiki-DPR

reproducibility.dataset_identity: nq_open validation questions 200-249; official DPR nq-test_gold_info source (the 3,610-question NQ-test population); Wiki-DPR psgs_w100.nq.compressed
reproducibility.environment: manifest records Python executable/version, git revision/status, config SHA-256, DPR URL/path/bytes/SHA-256, source scan count, corpus config, selection config, and seed

limitations: This is a diagnostic label-alignment audit, not a retrieval, selector, Generator, or utility intervention.
Strict coverage requires every official positive context to map uniquely, so it may intentionally be lower than any-positive coverage.
A coverage rate below 0.80 stops bottleneck classification; it does not establish that any production component is weak.
Full Wiki-DPR execution and source download are collaborator-side only.
